historical_commentary.text: Based on the available teaser, this note (third in an ongoing example-database series) demonstrates how to set up, manage, and run processes that are initiated/managed from a 4D Client but actually execute on the 4D Server, with conditional logic allowing the same code to run under single-user 4D or 4D Client as well. This general client/server process delegation pattern remains conceptually valid, but 4D has since introduced dedicated worker-process language commands (for managing background/server-side execution more directly and robustly) that address much of the same need with less manual plumbing than the technique this note likely demonstrates.
related_updates: 4D has since added dedicated worker-process commands (e.g., CALL WORKER and related process-management commands introduced in later versions) that provide a more direct, built-in way to run and manage background/server-side processes than manual client/server process orchestration
